features.name: Home page and configurable navigation
steps: Switch between Home, Queue, Inbox, Subscriptions, and More
The current entry is highlighted correctly
Open "Customize navigation" to reorder or hide entries
After confirming, the bottom bar/drawer shows the new structure
The configuration is preserved after a restart; the home-page sections can also be reorganized without changing business data
features.expected: The visibility and order of navigation entries must follow the custom configuration, and hidden entries must not appear again; the configuration is preserved after a restart; reorganizing the navigation or home-page sections must not affect business data such as subscriptions or the queue.

features.name: Search for and subscribe to a podcast
steps: Open "Add podcast"
Search the podcast directory
Open a search result
View the podcast and its episodes
Tap subscribe
The podcast enters the "Subscriptions" list
Opening the same podcast again shows the subscribed state instead of creating a duplicate subscription
features.expected: After a successful subscription the podcast must appear in the subscription list exactly once; opening an already-subscribed podcast again should show the subscribed state; the subscription relationship must persist and still exist after a restart.

features.name: Add a podcast via RSS address
steps: "Add podcast"
"Add podcast by RSS address"
Enter a valid feed address
Parse the title, cover, and episodes
The user confirms the subscription
Subscription and episode data are created
An invalid URL/invalid feed must not create a half-finished subscription. The official documentation also confirms that RSS/Atom feeds are an official way to add podcasts.
features.expected: The parsed result must come from the real feed content (title, cover, episodes); an invalid address or a parse failure must not create a subscription record; after confirming the subscription it must persist and be openable from the subscription list.

features.name: Local folder as a podcast
steps: Select "Add local folder"
Grant access to an audio directory
The local media appears as a browsable podcast/episode collection
After adding or deleting files in the directory a rescan reflects the changes
It does not depend on an internet feed
features.expected: The local folder content must genuinely generate playable episodes from the audio files; after adding or deleting files in the directory a rescan updates the result in sync; browsing still works without a network, and online feed data must not be faked.

features.name: Subscription refresh and new-episode discovery
steps: A subscribed feed
Refresh manually or reach the automatic refresh interval
Fetch the latest feed state
Only genuinely new episodes are added
New episodes enter the relevant list/inbox
Repeated refreshes must not create the same episode again. The official app refreshes periodically by default and allows changing the refresh interval.
features.expected: A refresh may only add genuinely new episodes, and repeated refreshes must not create duplicate episodes; local states of existing episodes such as downloads and playback progress must not be overwritten; a failed refresh must notify the user and not damage existing data.

features.name: Subscription list organization
steps: Multiple subscriptions exist
Change the list presentation through options such as filters, sorting, column count, counters, and title display
The sort/filter results are recomputed from real subscription data
Opening a podcast and returning keeps the context reasonably
features.expected: Sorting and filtering must genuinely change the list content and order rather than only the title; the column count and display options must take effect immediately and persist; after returning, the list context should be reasonably preserved.

features.name: Global search
steps: Enter search from pages such as Queue, Inbox, and Subscriptions
Enter keywords
Return matching results for the currently searchable data
Clearing the query restores the original page
No results and "the database is completely empty" use different states
features.expected: Search results must match real podcast or episode data; when nothing matches, show "no results" rather than an empty-database message; clearing the query should return to the page state from before entering search.

features.name: Inbox decision flow
steps: A feed refresh produces a new episode
The episode appears in the inbox

When the user ignores it, it is only removed from the inbox while the episode stays in the subscription; when the user adds it to the queue it leaves the inbox and enters the Queue; when the user downloads it, it also enters the downloading state and joins the queue according to the default behavior.
features.expected: The three decisions (ignore, add to queue, download) must produce distinct state results; ignoring must not delete the episode, and adding to the queue must create a queue relationship; after an operation the inbox counts and page states must update in sync.

features.name: Queue membership
steps: Use "Add to queue" from any episode page
The episode and the Queue establish a relationship
The queue's remaining episode count/total duration updates
Adding again must not create a duplicate queue entry
After removal from the queue the episode itself and the downloaded file still exist according to their own states
features.expected: The queue's remaining count and total duration must be computed from the real queue members; the same episode must not be enqueued twice; removing from the queue only releases the queue relationship and must not delete the episode or its downloaded file.

features.name: Queue order, sorting, and locking
steps: The queue contains episodes from multiple podcasts
Reorder manually by dragging
The next item to play changes with the order
The queue is rearranged after choosing a sort such as title/podcast/duration/date/random/Smart Shuffle
With locking or continuous sorting enabled manual adjustments are restricted
Unlocking restores them. The official documentation explicitly supports these sorting and locking semantics
features.expected: After dragging, the order must persist immediately and determine the next item to play; the sort mode must genuinely reorder the queue; with locking or continuous sorting enabled, manual dragging should be forbidden or overridden by automatic reordering, and restored after unlocking.

features.name: Player lifecycle and playback progress
steps: Open an episode
Play
The current time keeps advancing
Pause freezes it
Seek changes the playback position
Switching to another page and back keeps the player state
After exiting and reopening the episode, playback continues from the saved progress
Playback ends and enters the completed state
features.expected: The playback position must advance with real time and freeze after Pause; after Seek it continues from the new position; the progress must persist, and re-entering the same episode should resume rather than start over; finishing playback should mark it completed.

features.name: Fast-forward / rewind / playback speed
steps: Change the fast-forward seconds, rewind seconds, and allowed playback speeds in settings
During playback the buttons jump by the new values
After changing the speed the audio timeline advances at the new rate
The remaining time/media information affected by playback speed is recalculated in the UI
features.expected: Fast-forward and rewind must jump by the configured number of seconds and must not go past the file boundaries; a playback-speed change must genuinely affect the audio rate and the remaining-time display; the settings must persist and apply to all episodes.

features.name: System interruptions and playback control
steps: Enable "pause when headphones or Bluetooth disconnect"
Simulate a device disconnect during playback
Playback pauses automatically and keeps the current position
Reconnecting does not wrongly lose progress; after remapping the hardware forward/back buttons the corresponding player actions occur
features.expected: A disconnect event must trigger a pause and keep the playback position and must not reset progress; reconnecting should not wrongly lose or jump the progress; after remapping hardware buttons the corresponding player actions must be performed.

features.name: Continuous queue playback
steps: The queue is A
B
C
Play A to the end
A is handled as completed
B starts automatically
The queue pointer/remaining time update in sync
With "keep skipped episodes" enabled, Skip and normal completion produce different queue results
features.expected: After an episode ends it must automatically switch to the next one and be handled according to the completion policy, with the queue pointer and remaining duration updating in sync; when keeping skipped items is enabled, Skip and finishing must produce different queue results.

features.name: Manual download lifecycle
steps: Tap download on a not-yet-downloaded episode
It enters downloading
After success it appears on the "Downloads" page with local media state
It can play offline
Deleting the download only removes the media file rather than deleting the episode metadata
Download statistics change in sync
features.expected: Downloading and downloaded states must be distinguishable in lists; deleting a download only removes the local file while the episode and playback progress remain; download statistics and storage usage must update in sync and persist.

features.name: Automatic handling rules for new episodes
steps: Configure the podcast refresh interval and "new episode action" in download settings
When new feed items arrive they enter Inbox, Queue, or another configured state according to the rules
After a rule change only subsequently discovered episodes are affected; it should not rewrite all existing episodes
features.expected: Newly discovered episodes must enter the specified state according to the current rules; after changing the rules only subsequently discovered episodes are affected while existing episode states stay unchanged; the refresh interval must persist and actually control refresh timing.

features.name: Automatic download pipeline
steps: Enable global/podcast-level automatic download
Refresh and discover new episodes matching the rules
Download tasks are created automatically in the background
After success the episode leaves the inbox, joins the Queue, and appears in Downloads
Downloading should not continue unconditionally once count/network constraints are reached. The official documentation explicitly describes this cross-module chain.
features.expected: New episodes matching the rules must automatically start downloading and appear on the downloads page when finished; after success the inbox and queue states update in sync according to the configuration; downloading should stop when the count limit is exceeded or network conditions are not met.

features.name: Automatic deletion and space management
steps: Enable delete-after-playback or delete-when-low-on-space
After a downloaded episode finishes playing, the local media is removed according to the policy
With "remove from queue after deletion" enabled the queue changes in sync; with it disabled the two states stay independent
Protection conditions such as favorites/queue determine whether an item can be cleaned up according to the policy.
features.expected: After playback completes, the local media must be deleted according to the policy without deleting episode metadata; the "remove from queue after deletion" toggle must genuinely determine whether the queue changes in sync; protected items should not be cleaned up automatically.

features.name: Favorite relationship
steps: Mark an episode as favorite
It appears on the favorites page
The original subscription page/episode page shows the same favorite state
After unfavoriting from the favorites page the other pages sync
A favorite is not a copy of the episode but a persistent User–Episode relationship
features.expected: The favorite state must be consistent across all pages, and a change in any one place syncs everywhere; unfavoriting should not delete the episode or the downloaded file; the favorite relationship must persist across restarts.

features.name: Playback history
steps: The episode actually finishes playing / meets the completion condition
It appears in "Playback history"
Opening the record still links to the original episode
Clearing/removing history should not also delete subscriptions or media files
An empty history shows the corresponding empty state
features.expected: Only episodes that were actually played enter the history and link back to the original episode; clearing the history must not delete subscriptions, episodes, or downloaded files; when there are no records the corresponding empty state is shown.

features.name: Statistics and aggregated data
steps: Play different durations across several podcasts
Open statistics
"Subscriptions" aggregates playback duration by podcast
"Year" aggregates by month
"Downloads" shows the total media on the device

After new plays or download deletions the related numbers are recomputed rather than being a static chart. The official materials state that listening statistics are aggregated from each episode's played duration and last played.
features.expected: The statistics must be aggregated from real playback durations and download data and recomputed after new plays or deletions; the three dimensions (subscriptions, year, downloads) must be consistent with one another and must not show fixed sample values.

features.name: OPML subscription import / export
steps: Several subscriptions already exist
Export OPML
Import it in another empty/existing environment
Show the selectable podcasts
Only the selected items are added to the existing subscriptions and the original subscriptions are not overwritten
OPML only restores subscription relationships and does not fake playback progress, favorites, or queue data. The official documentation makes this difference clear.
features.expected: The exported OPML must contain the real subscription addresses; on import the existing subscriptions must not be overwritten and only the checked items are added; OPML cannot restore playback progress, favorites, or queue data.

features.name: Database backup and full restore
steps: Create a database backup
Afterwards change subscriptions, queue, favorites, playback state, and settings
Restore from the backup
These structures return to the backup point in time

Downloaded media must be fetched again rather than pretending to be restored along with the database. The official documentation defines database export as a full data migration method but makes clear that media must be downloaded again.
features.expected: After a restore, subscriptions, queue, favorites, playback state, and settings must return to the backup point in time; media files are not inside the backup and the downloaded state must not be faked after restoring; the restore should overwrite the current data rather than simply merge.
